declaration: R2 uses engine-truth reward and termination, so it is a training-time privileged diagnostic: it is NOT strict pixel self-improvement (R1) and no result here may be reported as R1.

supersedes.why: that run collected 0 episodes: collect_rollout reset the engine at every rollout, so no episode ever ended and no terminal reward ever reached PPO.  This run uses collect_rollout(resume=...) and finishes real episodes

round1_artefacts_preserved_as.note: the round-1 files were copied aside before this run wrote the canonical paths, so the first pilot's evidence stays attributable by sha

checkpoint_initial.warning: a second file with this name exists under T05/checkpoints and is a different model; reference by full path + sha256

death_penalty.counted: once per death, a first death does not end the episode

progress_total.unit: reward for traversing the whole first face by score
progress_total.counted: cumulative, hard-capped at progress_total per episode

progress_score_full.event: the score a real first-face clear reaches

survive_per_decision.unit: reward per decision at the two-frame beat
survive_per_decision.counted: 0.0: a bare survival constant is what §5 forbids, because at γ = 0.999833 (τ = 200 s) the discounted sum of a constant c is c/(1-γ) ≈ 6001·c and a long stall would out-earn a clear

progress_bound.meaning: a trajectory can never earn more than progress_total from progress, however long it stalls

floor.rule: the smallest τ in TAU_CANDIDATE_SECONDS whose γ^T at the measured clear length T = 6598 decisions reaches gamma_T_clear_min; ties broken towards the shorter effective horizon (the smaller τ)
floor.note: written before the revision ran and frozen after it; the thresholds are a visibility floor for a terminal event, not a tolerance that was moved to let a run through

discount.note: Δt = 2/60 s is the physical clock; τ = 200 s is the single diagnosed revision of the τ = 30 s initial configuration (at 30 s the terminal weight over the measured 6,598-decision clear was 6.55e-04, i.e. a clear bonus worth 1/382 of one death penalty). γ is always recomputed from Δt/τ and never read from the config

discount_floor.rule: written before the revision was applied and frozen after it: the smallest tau in [200, 300, 400, 600] whose gamma^T at the measured clear length reaches gamma_T_clear_min
discount_floor.note: the same floor as the audit config; a config may raise it but never lower it (resolve_discount_floor refuses relaxation)

terminal.note: a terminal reward only reaches PPO on a terminated transition, so both counters have to be > 0 for a training run to be about the task objective at all

trained: critic (Linear(128,1) on the frozen trunk output)

terminal.note: a terminal reward only reaches PPO on a terminated transition, so both counters have to be > 0 for a training run to be about the task objective at all

arithmetic.labelled: planning arithmetic only — NOT a result and NOT a schedule promise
arithmetic.basis: this run's measured wall throughput including updates, plus one engine restart per episode at the frozen evaluator's own 6.5 s
arithmetic.why_it_is_not_claimed: round 1 extrapolated 1M from a run whose episode count was 0, so its per-episode restart term was a fallback rather than a measurement.  This tier measured real episodes but still only 50k frames and one seed, so a 1M schedule has to be re-derived from a run with the corrected wiring instead of being promised here

R0.provenance: measured in T04 with the same frozen evaluator, the same 20 dev seeds and the same checkpoint sha256; reshaped here, not re-run
R0.not_re_run: deterministic argmax on the same checkpoint sha, the same frozen evaluator, the same engine and the same 20 dev seeds; the T04 measurement is the frozen record

notes: R2 uses engine-truth reward and termination, so it is a training-time privileged diagnostic: it is NOT strict pixel self-improvement (R1) and no result here may be reported as R1.
one seed at a 50,000-frame budget is a pilot: it is not the 1M-frame tier and a single seed is not three
the frozen ruler evaluates the trained checkpoint in argmax mode, so the deployment rule is the same one R0 is measured with
episode count > 0 and terminated transitions > 0 are the two numbers that prove a terminal reward actually entered PPO in this run

seed_reporting.why: collect_rollout read the seed out of the rebuilt StepResult.info, and a rebuilt StepResult only carries env.info(), which has no seed field, so an episode that ended after its first decision recorded 0
seed_reporting.derivation: with 24 finished episodes, episode i used train_seeds[i % 5], i.e. 3000,3001,3002,3003,3004,3000,... — all inside the train pool (3000-3004) and none inside the dev (1000-1019) or confirm (61000-61499) windows
seed_reporting.fix: collect_rollout now tracks the seed it reset with, writes it into the episode record and into the resume carry, and test_resume_keeps_one_episode_running_so_resets_are_fewer_than_rollouts asserts episodes[0]['seed'] == 3000
seed_reporting.measurements_unchanged: a bookkeeping field only: the seed passed to env.reset() is the same value before and after the fix, so no trajectory, update or checkpoint in this payload is affected; the payload itself is NOT rewritten
